subject: Re: Aurora - sizing stretch & GPU price contingency for reserved plan
messages:
From: Erica Park <erica@aurora-ai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aurora-ai.com
Date: 2027-03-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Aurora RFP - reserved capacity ask and pricing sensitivity

Hi Tessa and Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Aurora is finalizing numbers for our Q3 inference rollout and procurement asked me to send the RFP (attached) and call out two things we need clarity on before we go to legal:

1) Sizing flex: we expect initial steady-state of ~120k token-rps but early months could spike to ~250k token-rps due to pilot bursts. How does Redwood handle short-duration oversubscribe? Do reserved pools allow temporary burst credits without renegotiating the commitment?

2) GPU cost contingency: procurement is concerned about price movement for GPUs across the 12–24 month term. Are there mechanisms for price pass-through or conditional discounts if our committed token volumes are reduced due to price shocks?

Attached: Aurora_RFP_Q3.pdf.

Can we get a short write-up and any example contract clause language by end of week? Legal wants to include contingencies in the draft MPA.

Best,
Erica
Procurement | Aurora AI

--
Attachment: Aurora_RFP_Q3.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Erica Park <erica@aurora-ai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-25T13:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Aurora RFP - reserved capacity ask and pricing sensitivity

Erica — thanks for sending and for the clear ask. Quick summary below; Marcus and I will flesh this out into contract language and cost scenarios.

Sizing stretch (short answer): we support a tiered burst model. Reserved pools include configured burst capacity (percentage-based) for short windows; beyond that, we offer a one-time pool expansion call with a pre-agreed ramp/delta price. Customers can also buy short-term burst credits at pre-negotiated rates to avoid immediate re-commit.

GPU price contingency (short answer): we typically give fixed committed pricing for the contract term, but for 18–24 month deals we'll include a GPU-price-sensitivity clause that allows either (a) a 90-day renegotiation trigger if hardware-hour costs move >X%, or (b) an indexed adjustment tied to a published GPU index with caps. We usually put a floor/ceiling to avoid wide swings.

I'll loop in Laura for procurement/legal clauses and Marcus for SKU/ops risk. We can aim to deliver a redline and a couple of pricing scenarios by Thursday 31 Mar.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 84KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Erica Park <erica@aurora-ai.com>
Date: 2027-03-26T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Aurora RFP - reserved capacity ask and pricing sensitivity

Adding technical/ops context from the fleet planning side:

- Burst model specifics: we can configure per-customer burst pools up to 2.5x baseline for windows up to 72 hours without shifting baseline runbooks. Beyond that, autoscale will pull from shared spare capacity which is priced at a higher e-rate. We recommend embedding an explicit burst credit allowance (e.g., 1M tokens/day at 1.8x) in the MPA for the pilot phase.
- Lead times: provisioning additional dedicated nodes for sustained increases takes 10–12 business days (hardware + provisioning). For faster needs we can offer ephemeral instances routed to shared-hosted runners with encrypted KV caching; that has different SLAs.
- Operational risk: if Aurora wants committed physical SKUs (specific GPU families), we can offer price-locks but it increases risk and requires a longer lead time on allocation.

I'll draft a short operations appendix that outlines burst mechanics and provisioning timelines.

-Marcus
VP, Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Erica Park <erica@aurora-ai.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Aurora RFP - reserved capacity ask and pricing sensitivity

Erica — attaching an initial legal-friendly clause set and three pricing scenarios (conservative, baseline, aggressive). Key highlights:

- Contingency clause option A (index-triggered): if the GPU hardware index published monthly moves outside +/- 12% for three consecutive months, either party may request good-faith renegotiation of unit pricing; any change requires mutual written consent.
- Contingency clause option B (volume shield): if Aurora’s committed monthly token usage falls >30% versus baseline for a rolling 3-month window due to market price shocks, Aurora may reduce committed capacity by up to one tier with a stepped termination fee scaled to remaining term.
- Burst credits: we recommend a pilot allowance of 2M tokens/month of burst credits for 90 days, convertible to committed units at a preferential rate if converted within the pilot.

See attached proposed-mpa-Aurora.docx for redlines. Happy to take feedback.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel | Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: proposed-mpa-Aurora.docx (document, 45KB)

From: Erica Park <erica@aurora-ai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aurora-ai.com, Ben Chu <ben.chu@aurora-ai.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Aurora RFP - reserved capacity ask and pricing sensitivity

Thanks all — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement/CTO:

- The +/-12% index-trigger looks reasonable, but procurement would prefer a 6% threshold for the first six months to reduce early volatility risk. Could you run cost scenarios that show price to Aurora under 6%, 12%, and 20% shocks over 12 months?
- For burst credits: can you confirm if unused burst credits at month-end roll into a quarter pool or expire? Aurora prefers some rollover into the next month or quarter to smooth unpredictability.
- On the volume shield: legal asks that the stepped termination fee be quantitatively defined in the doc (e.g., X months of committed spend).

Also copying Ben — he wants to understand implications if we lock specific GPU SKUs now and GPU spot/market declines unexpectedly.

Look forward to the scenarios by Thursday.

-Erica

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Erica Park <erica@aurora-ai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Chu <ben.chu@aurora-ai.com>, procurement@aurora-ai.com
Date: 2027-04-02T17:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Aurora RFP - reserved capacity ask and pricing sensitivity

Erica and team — we ran scenarios and put numbers into the attached sheet. Quick notes:

- Scenario outputs: included three shock curves (6%, 12%, 20%). For Aurora’s baseline profile the delta to monthly committed spend ranges from +4.2% (6% shock) to +13.9% (20% shock) under index-trigger adjustments with our proposed floor/ceiling caps.
- Rollover: pilot burst credits will roll up into a quarterly pool for the first 90 days; after that unused credits expire month-to-month unless converted to committed units.
- Termination fee: proposed stepped fee = remaining committed months * 25% of monthly committed spend (scales down after 12 months). We put an example calculation on tab "Termination-Examples".
- SKU lock: if Aurora requires SKU-level price-locks we recommend a 6–8 week procurement lead and a 7% premium on committed price as an allocation risk premium. If Aurora wants to avoid SKU lock, the indexed approach is simpler and cheaper overall.

Next steps: 1) Laura to mark the preferred contingency option in the MPA redline; 2) Erica/Ben to confirm preferred shock threshold (6% vs 12%); 3) Marcus will finalize the burst provisioning appendix.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
